title: The Poker Legend Behind Taylor Sheridan's Four Sixes Ranch
description:
Taylor Sheridan is in the news this week, and so is his famous Texas ranch, the Four Sixes. Legend says it was won in a poker game with a hand of four sixes. The real story starts with a hundred head of cattle, a Comanche friendship and a president's wolf hunt.
🚶 Visiting San Diego? Explore its history on a guided tour with Fable: https://fablehospitality.com

Every frame is drawn with code. No stock footage, no AI video.

0:48 About 150 years in the family, then sold
0:54 A hundred cows and a brand

Note: sources give 1868 or 1870 for Burnett's first purchase of the 6666 herd (from Frank Crowley of Denton County), so the video says "around 1870". Theodore Roosevelt wrote in 1905 that Burnett's Four Sixes brand "has been owned by him for forty years." The poker-game story is folklore that Burnett and his descendants have always denied. The sale to the group led by Taylor Sheridan was announced in 2022 (some sources date the deal to 2021); the price was not disclosed.

Images (public domain): "At the Tail of the Chuck Wagon" (photograph by W. Sloan Simpson) and "Starting Towards the Wolf Grounds" (photograph by Alexander Lambert), from Theodore Roosevelt, Outdoor Pastimes of an American Hunter (1905, Internet Archive); portrait of S. B. Burnett from B. B. Paddock, History of Texas: Fort Worth and the Texas Northwest Edition, vol. 3 (1922, Internet Archive); "Quanah Parker" from James T. DeShields, Cynthia Ann Parker: The Story of Her Capture (1886, Internet Archive). Playing cards and documents drawn in code.
Maps drawn in code from Natural Earth (world-atlas) and US Census (us-atlas) outlines.
Narration voice is synthetic.
